subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Heating a substance without changing its state increases its internal energy. Specifically, it increases the particles'...
options: potential energy only, so temperature stays constant
number
kinetic energy, so the temperature rises
mass
questions.explain: When heating raises temperature (no state change), the energy increases the particles' kinetic energy, so they move faster and the temperature rises.

questions.q: What is the role of a step-down transformer in the national grid?
options: It increases the current in the transmission cables
It decreases the p.d. to a safe value for homes
It converts ac to dc
It increases the p.d. before transmission
questions.explain: A step-down transformer reduces the high transmission potential difference to a safer, lower value (about 230 V) for use in homes. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. for transmission.

questions.q: What is the specific latent heat of vaporisation of a substance?
options: The energy to change the state of 1 kg from liquid to gas with no temperature change
The energy to change the state of 1 kg from solid to liquid
The energy to raise 1 kg by 1°C
The energy to melt 1 g of the substance
questions.explain: Specific latent heat of vaporisation is the energy needed to change 1 kg of a substance from liquid to gas (or back) at constant temperature. Latent heat of fusion refers to the solid↔liquid change.

questions.q: What is nuclear fusion?
options: Two light nuclei joining to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
A nucleus emitting an alpha particle
An electron joining the nucleus
A large unstable nucleus splitting into two smaller nuclei
questions.explain: Fusion is the joining of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy (as in the Sun). Fission is the splitting of a large unstable nucleus into smaller ones.

questions.q: Why does the national grid use step-up transformers before transmission over long distances?
options: To increase the current and reduce the voltage
To increase the voltage and reduce the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
To convert ac to dc for transmission
To make the cables thicker
questions.explain: Stepping up the p.d. reduces the current for the same power (P = VI). Lower current means much less energy wasted as heat in the resistance of the transmission cables (heating ∝ I²R).

questions.q: A child slides down a slide and ends up moving more slowly than a frictionless calculation predicts. Where has the 'missing' energy gone?
options: Dissipated as thermal energy by friction
Converted entirely to sound
Stored as extra chemical energy
It has been destroyed
questions.explain: Energy is conserved and cannot be destroyed. Friction dissipates energy to the thermal store of the slide and surroundings, so less reaches the kinetic store.

questions.q: Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays can be dangerous to living cells mainly because they are:
options: Too slow to escape the body
Very low frequency
Forms of sound
Ionising, so they can damage cells and DNA and cause cancer
questions.explain: UV, X-rays and gamma rays carry high energy and are ionising. They can damage cells and mutate DNA, increasing the risk of cancer; radiation dose is measured in sieverts (Sv).

questions.q: Which energy resource is most reliable for continuous large-scale electricity generation?
options: Wind
Fossil fuels
Solar
Wave
questions.explain: Fossil-fuel power stations can run on demand at any time, making them reliable, whereas solar, wind and wave depend on the weather and time of day.

questions.q: What makes a main sequence star (like the Sun) stable for billions of years?
options: There are no forces acting on it
The inward force of gravity is balanced by the outward pressure from fusion energy
It is constantly shrinking
It is held together by magnetism
questions.explain: During the main sequence the inward pull of gravity is balanced by the outward force from the expansion of hot gases (energy released by hydrogen fusion). This equilibrium keeps the star stable.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between energy and power?
options: Energy and power are the same quantity
Energy is measured in watts; power in joules
Power is energy stored; energy is the rate of transfer
Power is the rate at which energy is transferred
questions.explain: Power is the energy transferred per second (P = E/t), measured in watts; energy is measured in joules. Confusing the two is a common error.

questions.q: What was Bohr's key contribution to the development of the atomic model?
options: He suggested electrons orbit the nucleus at specific fixed distances (energy levels)
He proposed the plum pudding model
He fired alpha particles at gold foil
He discovered the proton
questions.explain: Bohr adapted the nuclear model by proposing that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances (energy levels), which matched experimental observations.

questions.q: Why did scientists propose the existence of dark matter and dark energy?
options: To explain the colour of stars
To replace the Big Bang theory
Because the universe contains no ordinary matter
To explain observations (such as galaxy motion and accelerating expansion) that ordinary matter alone cannot account for
questions.explain: Observations of how galaxies move and how the universe's expansion is speeding up cannot be explained by visible matter alone, so scientists proposed dark matter and dark energy. There is still much we do not understand about them.

questions.q: For an object (such as the Earth) to stay at a constant temperature, what must be true about its radiation?
options: It neither absorbs nor emits radiation
It emits more radiation than it absorbs
The rate it absorbs radiation equals the rate it emits radiation
It absorbs more radiation than it emits
questions.explain: Temperature stays constant when the power absorbed equals the power emitted. If absorption exceeds emission the object warms; if emission exceeds absorption it cools.

questions.q: In the national grid, what is the role of a step-down transformer near homes?
options: To raise the voltage for long-distance transmission
To convert ac to dc
To lower the voltage to a safer level for domestic use
To increase the current in the transmission lines
questions.explain: Step-up transformers raise the voltage for efficient transmission; step-down transformers near towns and homes lower the voltage (e.g. to 230 V) so it is safe to use in buildings.

questions.q: What is meant by the internal energy of a system?
options: The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles
The energy supplied by an external heater
Only the kinetic energy of the particles
Only the potential energy stored between particles
questions.explain: Internal energy is the total energy stored by the particles: the sum of their kinetic energy (from motion) and the potential energy stored in the bonds/forces between them.

questions.q: What will happen to the Sun (a low-mass star) when it runs low on hydrogen fuel?
options: It will become a black hole
It will become a neutron star
It will explode as a supernova
It will expand into a red giant, then become a white dwarf
questions.explain: A low-mass star like the Sun swells into a red giant, then sheds its outer layers and the core becomes a white dwarf that slowly cools.

questions.q: A student says 'current is used up as it goes round a series circuit, so the second lamp is dimmer.' Why is this wrong?
options: Current is only in the first half of the circuit
Current increases round a series circuit
Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
Current is voltage divided by charge
questions.explain: Current is the rate of flow of charge and is the same at every point in a single series loop. Charge (and current) is not 'used up'; energy is transferred from the potential difference.

questions.q: What do all waves transfer from one place to another?
options: Electrons
Mass
Matter
Energy (and information), not matter
questions.explain: Waves transfer energy (and information) without transferring matter. The particles or fields oscillate about a fixed position; they are not carried along with the wave.

questions.q: During the main sequence stage, what process releases energy in a star's core?
options: Gravitational collapse only
Nuclear fission of uranium
Burning of fuel like a fire (combustion)
Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
questions.explain: Main sequence stars release energy by nuclear fusion, joining hydrogen nuclei to form helium. This is not chemical burning — it is a nuclear process in the core.

questions.q: What is the activity of a radioactive source?
options: The mass of the source
The energy of each emitted particle
The number of undecayed nuclei remaining
The rate at which its nuclei decay, measured in becquerel (Bq)
questions.explain: Activity is the rate at which nuclei of a source decay, measured in becquerel (Bq), where 1 Bq is one decay per second.

questions.q: On a heating graph, the temperature stays constant while a substance boils. What is happening to the energy supplied during this flat section?
options: It is being used to increase the particles' kinetic energy
It is being lost and has no effect
It is being used to break the bonds between particles (increasing potential energy)
It is reducing the mass of the substance
questions.explain: During a change of state the temperature is constant because the energy supplied breaks the bonds/forces between particles (raising potential energy), not their kinetic energy.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph, what does the gradient of the straight (linear) region represent?
options: The weight of the spring
The spring constant
The elastic potential energy
The limit of proportionality
questions.explain: For the linear region, F = ke, so the gradient (force ÷ extension) is the spring constant k. The area under the line gives the elastic potential energy stored.
